subject: Use RCytoscape to display  'legend'  (i.e., informational) nodes

messages.author: a54722eec6bfa845
messages.subject: Use RCytoscape to display  'legend'  (i.e., informational) nodes
parts:
I have just added a cookbook recipe (some simple code accompanied by
explanations) for adding a 'legend node' to your display.

To quote from the recipe:

In traditional use of Cytoscape, every node is a 'data' node: it
represents a molecule or a process, or some other analytical entity.
Just as in map-making, we sometimes want more. You may wish to put up
a legend, or some explanatory text, perhaps a prominent label saying,
i.e.,

"Time point 3 (8 hours)"
"Low Oxygen"
"Patient 5"
Here is how to do that. As usual, I demonstrate this in the context of
the makeSimpleGraph () (see 'methods' for more information about this
built-in RCytoscape utility function).
g = RCytoscape::makeSimpleGraph ()
g = graph::addNode ('info.node', g)
nodeData (g, 'info.node', 'label') = 'information will be written
here'
window.title = 'Legend Demo'
cw = new.CytoscapeWindow (window.title, graph=g)
displayGraph (cw)
layout (cw, "jgraph-spring")
redraw (cw)

# now set up the appearance of the informational node, using a bunch
of 'direct' calls
setNodeShapeDirect (cw, 'info.node', 'rect')
setNodeSizeDirect (cw, 'info.node', 140)
setNodeFontSizeDirect (cw, 'info.node', 32);
setNodeLabelDirect (cw, 'info.node', '')
setNodeColorDirect (cw, 'info.node', '#FFEEFF')
fitContent (cw)
redraw (cw)

# now change and update the message in the information node a few
times
for (i in 1:10) {
random.int = as.integer (100 * runif (1))
new.label = paste ('random label', random.int)
setNodeLabelDirect (cw, 'info.node', new.label)
redraw (cw)
system ('sleep 1')
}
